reviews.title: DON’T PANIC ABOUT THE BIOS, HERE IS HOW TO GET ROCK SOLID STABILITY
reviews.comment:
I BOUGHT THIS SPECIFICALLY BECAUSE I WANTED MODERN CONNECTIVITY AND BUILD QUALITY WITHOUT THE EXPENSE OF DDR5 RAM. The main appeal of this board is getting WiFi 6 and USB-C at excellent value for money, but the fear with budget boards is often that they feel cheap or flimsy. Surprisingly, the VRM heatsinks have substantial weight and the overall looks are very clean, offering the kind of stability you usually only find on much more expensive models. It handles power delivery perfectly, but you have to get it running first, which brings me to the critical setup step.
The manual makes the Q-Flash Plus feature sound like it offers instant ease of use, but here is the reality check to avoid connection issues. You cannot just drag and drop the BIOS file; you must format your USB drive to FAT32 and rename the file to gigabyte.bin or the board will simply ignore it. Once I did this rename trick, the functionality was flawless and the system has been completely stable with my XMP memory profiles enabled ever since. If you skip this step, the process will fail, and you might mistakenly think the board is defective.
The only real downside regarding the fit is that the mATX size is naturally compact. If you have large hands or a massive air cooler, the port size for the top CPU power cable can be tight to reach, though the PCIe EZ-Latch definitely makes swapping the GPU easier. However, having reliable Bluetooth connectivity and robust features in this small form factor makes it a fantastic choice. Overall, if you want high-end performance and features on a budget, this is a smart buy as long as you prep your USB drive correctly.
reviews.author: Matthew Hewitt

reviews.title: GIGABYTE B760M Gaming Plus WiFi DDR4 – The perfect “just works” budget rocket ship for 13th/14th-gen
reviews.comment:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
GIGABYTE B760M Gaming Plus WiFi DDR4 – The perfect “just works” budget rocket ship for 13th/14th-gen Intel
Built a screaming-fast daily driver/gaming rig for my nephew using this board + i5-14400F + 32GB DDR4-3600 + RX 7800 XT and it’s been rock-solid for 5 months now. Paid $129 on sale and honestly feels like I stole something.
Why this board punches way above its price
Real 12+1+1 phase DrMOS VRM with decent heatsinks – running my 14400F at unlimited power limits 24/7 (200W+ sustained) and VRM temps never crack 58 °C even in Prime95
DDR4 support saved him $120 vs buying new DDR5 sticks (hit 4000 MHz CL16 XMP out of the box, zero stability issues)
Built-in WiFi 6E + Bluetooth 5.3 (Intel AX210 module) pulls 1.3 Gbps next to my router and has rock-solid 6 GHz band performance
2.5 GbE LAN (Intel i225-V) – no Realtek nonsense here
Four M.2 slots (one PCIe 4.0 x4 right off the CPU, the others PCIe 3.0) – already has a 2 TB Gen4 boot drive + 4 TB Gen3 storage, still two slots free
BIOS is idiot-proof: Q-Flash Plus (update BIOS without CPU/RAM), XMP one-click, fan curves super easy
I/O is actually useful
Rear: USB-C 20 Gbps, USB 3.2 Gen2, HDMI + DP for iGPU, clear CMOS button (lifesaver when he inevitably overclocks too far).
Front header: USB-C Gen2x2 (he’s using it for a 10-bay dock).
Build quality & little touches
Matte black PCB + silver heatsinks looks clean in a white case
Pre-installed I/O shield
Debug LED + onboard power/reset buttons
Zero coil whine, zero cold-boot issues even at -20 °F Michigan winters
Only two nitpicks (and they’re tiny):
Only one full-speed PCIe x16 slot (fine for 99 % of people, but no room for 10GbE + GPU if you’re crazy)
Only 4 SATA ports (again, who uses more than two in 2025?)
For $129-149 this board is stupidly good. I was about to buy him an ASUS Prime B760M-A WiFi D4, but this GIGABYTE has better VRMs, better LAN, an extra M.2, and cost $30 less. Already built two more identical rigs for friends who saw his 14400F crushing 7800X3D builds in games for half the price.
If you still have fast DDR4 lying around and want a 14th-gen board that just works, overclocks decently, and won’t die when you push PL2 to infinity, buy this thing before the price goes back up. 10/10, GIGABYTE absolutely nailed the budget B760 formula here.
reviews.author: DeLawders

reviews.title: Solid DDR4 Board with Stable Performance and Good Connectivity
reviews.comment:
Installed the GIGABYTE B760M Gaming Plus WiFi DDR4 in a compact micro-ATX build paired with a 13th Gen Intel processor and 32GB DDR4 memory. The board booted without issues, and BIOS navigation was straightforward for initial setup.
Memory compatibility has been stable using XMP, and the system has remained consistent under gaming and productivity workloads. VRM cooling appears adequate for mid-range CPUs, and temperatures stayed within normal limits during stress testing.
Built-in WiFi connected immediately without driver complications, and overall connectivity options are well laid out for a board in this size category. M.2 installation was simple, and PCIe slots feel reinforced and secure.
For builders who want to continue using DDR4 while upgrading to newer Intel platforms, this motherboard offers a balanced mix of features, stability, and value without unnecessary extras.
Overall, a dependable choice for a performance-focused micro-ATX build.
reviews.author: George

reviews.title: Great motherboard!
reviews.comment:
Great board! Booted right up with an i5 12600k, WiFi and Bluetooth drivers needed to be installed after windows installed and booted to desktop,  ethernet/LAN may or may not work out of the box(I use WiFi so I skipped the internet connection setup during the windows/account setup before booting to deksktop) I did the test the system hardwired and it works great!
There is no usb c port on the motherboard I/O in the back but there is a usb 3.0 and usb c connector on the board itself if you use a case that has a usb c on the case I/O
Bluetooth and WiFi connectivity are great, bios update was easy! Very nice little board with decent bios customization
Doesn’t have a dedicated aio  pump connector so I ran my pump off the cpu fan header,it does have a decent amount of headers though !
